items.title: Harrison Verrett Interview, 1961-08-10
items.q: Well, no, I saw him in Los Angeles there in 58... Before he left to go to California, we went to his house with him back in Carrollton, back in Hollygrove.

ctx.x: Yeah, he stood here quite a while. I used to rehearse with him. He called me up and would go up to his house and we'd sit on it. He had two six-string banjos. He promised me one I didn't pick up on at the time, so he gave it away to someone else. He's a wonderful banjo musician too. I saw him in New York in 59. I spent a couple days with him at his house.
Did you ever hear Johnny St. Sarah much in the old days?

Well, no, I saw him in Los Angeles there in 58. He'd come to the hotel where he was, you know, but I never... One of the one time here, let's see, it's been... Before he left to go to California, we went to his house with him back in Carrollton, back in Hollygrove. We went back there one night, one evening, and they had a lot. We called it a jam. We called it a booze, that's what the Creoles call it, you know. We like to drink. What's that word? They call it a booze. That's what the Creoles call it here. Booze.…
